fer beyde, und beyder fernieren an

henden Ratis zu bezahlen, nämlich
zu Johann Baptiste a. c. 4000 Rt

seiner hochfürstl. Durchlaucht leisten

im Blesitz habenden, und ihnen bey der
tradition
Tradition zu übergebenden Grund
stücke Eviction in Ansehung der

so von der Bürgerschaft zu War¬
ta evincirt werden können, und

durchlaucht befinden wird keine Evi¬

fälligen Aecker auf ihre ganz

die Uebergabe dieses verkauf¬
ten Guths an die Käufer soll 14
Tage nach Johanni a. c. erfolgen
bey welcher zugleich zug und zur
die erste Rathe der 4000 rtll.
bezahlt werden muß, weil ehr
dieses geschehen die Uebergabe
nicht erfolgen kann.

Bey dieser Uebergabe wird das
jenige Grund zuverloren und Vieh¬
und Geratschaften mit übergeben
was auf dem Guthe befindlich
ist und in dem Gerichtl. Uebergabe
Receß abseiten des Pächter Knob¬
lauch an den v Bloch auf Blotniz

nicht mehr befindlich sind, und
eben daher nicht mit übergeben

sens zur Acquisition dieses Guts
der Käufer wo möglich späte.
stens als Johann a. c. zu beschaf¬
fen, sollte derselbe aber nicht
erfolgen, so gehet der diesfälli¬
ge Kauf zurück.

gen des diesfälligen Contentes
langer als 14 Tage bis nach Jo¬
hann a. c. sich vergegern, derge¬
stallt, daß die Uebergabe bereits
erfolgt und die erste Rathe
des Kauf-Pretii bereits bezahlt
seyn sollte, alsdann aber die
diesfällige Resolution abschläglich
mesfallen
ausfallen, so sind Contrahenten
zu Vermeidung aller Bewesungen
wegen der erhebenen Revenuis
dahin übereingekommen, daß
Käufer dieses Guth ein Jahr lang
nämlich bis 14 Tage nach St. Jo¬
hanni 1804. Pachtweise in Besitz
behalten, dagegen über für die¬
ses Jahr ein Pacht quantum
von 800 rtl. sage Acht hundert
Reichsthaler an Herrn Ver¬
ckäufer bezahlen, auch sämtl.
öffentliche Abgaben dieses
Guth betreffend solche mögen
Nahmen haben, wie sie wollen
auf die Competenz ex Propri¬
et entrichten ohne dem Herrn
Verkäufer dafür Etwas in
Anrechnung bringen zu der
fen, und begeben sich Käufer
auf diesen lezten Fall aller
und jeder sonst Remissionen
und sonstigen Forderungen
solche haben Nahmen wie sie
wollen, sondern verbinden
sich bey der bereitesten Execu¬
tion das Guth Witow 14 Tage
nach Johann 1804 in wirth¬
schriftl. guten Stande zu räumen
und unterwerfen sich dieser
halb
halb dem Executiv Process mit

Räumen des Guths die bezahlten

irten Pacht-Pension von 800 rt

Abgeben und Kosten, die sie
beym Abzuge nicht als bezahlt

wöllig bestellter Vater und Sem¬
mer-Saat übergeben, und er¬
klären Käufer hiebey, daß sie
die Winter-Saat für gehörig
bestellt annehmen, und nur
noch an Gleiches in Ansehung der
Sümmerung erwarten.

Documente sollen den Käufern
gleich nach Eingang des Consen¬
ses zu ihrer Aequisitions

zuviederlaufenden Einwendungen

sage sie tausend Reichsthaler
welche der contraveniende Theil

contract gleichwohl zu erstellen
verbunden seyn soll

Nahmen der Künfern leztere
allein.

ihnen selbst dem gelesene Kauf¬
Punctalion welche den Mitkäufer
v Kwasiborski von seinem Socio
Honricht in pohleischer Sprache
explicirt werden, nach ver¬
ganziger
gängiger Genehmigung dem
ihre eigenhändige Nahmens
Unterschriften willzogen.
Kalisch den 21ten April: 1803.
er der Unterschrift bemerckten mich
beyde Theile, daß in Ansehung der auf

die dasigen Pächter selbst gebaut haben
wollen, den Käufern vom Herrn Verkäufer
keine Eviction geleistet wird, sondern
im Fall die Angabe der Pächter richtig
seyn sollte, Käufer sich deshalb mit ihnen
besonders abzufinden haben.

Die nach vorstehender Kauf Punctation mir in Termino
Weihnachten d. J. zu bezahlenden 6000 rl. Sechs Tau¬
send Reichsthaler Kauf Gelder, deßgleichen von
den in Termino Johannis 1804. zahlbaren 6000 rt
ein quantum von Zwei Tausend Reichsthler, mit
Prioritaet vor dem Residuo, auch mit allen Rech¬
ten und ohne Neuerung, und mit dem in dem
künftig zu errichtenden Kaufs Instrumen¬
te zu bedingenden, bei Eintragung des Be¬
siz-Titels zu interbulirenden Pfand-Rechte,
und mit Zinsen zu 5. procent von Johann¬
nis c. an, cedire ich hiermit an den
hiesiger Banquier Herrn Carl Ferdinand
Weigel. Ich bekenne, die Valuta dieser
Cession von demselben baar und richtig
erhalten zu haben.
Auch verspreche
ich, dem Herrn Banquier Weigel die Ein¬
willigung der Schuldner in diese Cession
bald möglichst zu verschaffen.
Breslau den 26ten April 1803.
Friedrich Ludwig Fürst zu Hohenlohe
selbst gelesen und genehmiget.
Vorstehende Cession, Quittung über die Valu¬
ta und das Versprechen der zu verschaf¬
fenden Einwilligung der Debitorum accep¬
tire ich im Nahmen und als Compagnon mei¬
nes Vaters Carl Ferdinand Weigel.
Breslau den 26ten April 1803.
ich habe dieses gelesen und genehmigt
Carl Gottlieb Weigel
im Nahmen und als Compagnon seines Vaters
Carl Ferdinand Weigel
Daß vorstehende Cession und Quittung über die
Valuta von des Herrn Friedrich Ludewig re¬
gierenden Fürsten zu Hohenlohe-Ingel¬
fingen Hochfürstl. Durchlaucht, und die von
dem Herrn Kaufmann Carl Gottlieb
Weigel, im Nahmen und als Compagnon seines
Vaters Herrn Carl Ferdinand Weigel erklährt
te Acceptation, unter heutigem Dato vor
dem Justiz Amte des Frauen Fürstl. Stifts
zu S. Vincenz, welchem dieselben persönlich
wohl bekannt sind, nach geschehener Durch¬
lesung und erklährter Genehmigung durch
Ihre eigenhändige Nahmens Unterschrif¬
ten und beigefügte Siegel, so wohl auf
dieser Original Punctation, als auf der
dem Herrn Cessionario ertheilten vidimirten
Abschrift derselben, vollzogen worden,
wird, auf den Grund [..ors?] hierüber auf
genommenen Protocolls hiermit attestirt
Breslau den 26 April 1803
Des Justiz-Amt des Frauen Fürstl. Stift zu
Vincenz
[L. S.]

Kwasieborski, als Käufern am andern Theil ist Behufs eines in der Folge wegen des Adelichen Guths Witow abzuschließenden förmlichen gerichtlichen Kauf und Verkauf-Con tracks nachstehende Punctation unterm heutigen dato wohlbedachtig verabredet, und abgeschloßen werden.

Südpreysch. E. W. v. Rösch. Between the Special Plenipotentiary of thy Most Serene Highness the reigning Lord Fürst zu Hohenlohe Ingelfingen, Herr Forest Inspector Rochlitz, as seller on the one part, and Herr Martin Honrichs and Herr Valentin v. Kwasieborski as purchasers on the other part, there is, for the purpose of a formal judicial contract of purchase and sale to be concluded hereafter concerning the noble estate of Witow, the following Punctation agreed upon and concluded under this day's date after mature deliberation.

The said Herr Forest Inspector Rochlitz sells, in the name of His Most Serene Highness the reigning Lord Fürst zu Hohenlohe Ingelfingen, the aforesaid, his Lord Principal's noble estate situated in the Royal South Prussian Kalisch Government Department and its Warta district, namely the village and Scholtisey Witow, with all rights and appurtenances thereto pertaining, nothing thereof excepted, in such wise as the same, pursuant to the Most High deed of donation [uncertain: Donations-Urkunde] of the most blessed King Frie-

-drich Wilhelm the Second, [uncertain: were granted to] Colonel v. Schlieben, and were conveyed by his widow and heirs, pursuant to the judicial contract of purchase of the 22nd of October 1799, to thy Most Serene Highness; unto the said Herr Martin Honrichs and Valentin v. Kwasieborski, and this indeed for a purchase price agreed and determined between the contracting parties after mature deliberation of 16000 rt, written out sixteen thousand Reichsthaler Prussian Courant.

2. This purchase price the purchasers bind themselves to pay in solidum, that is to say, one for both and both for one [uncertain], to His Most Serene Highness in the following instalments, namely at Johannes Baptista a. c. 4000 Rt, say four thousand Reichsthaler; at [uncertain: Weihnachten] a. c. 6000 rtl., say six thousand Reichsthaler; and at Johanni 1804 the remainder with 6000 rt., say six thousand Reichsthaler; and until the full payment of the arrears to pay interest upon the same at 5 per cent.

3. His Most Serene Highness grants to the purchasers Eviction warranty only for the parcels actually in possession and to be handed over to them at the

tradition. In respect of those 1016 Skladen of arable land which may be [uncertain: recovered] by the burghership of Warta, and which are not in the possession of thy Most Serene Highness, no warranty of Eviction is granted; rather it remains the purchasers' business alone to vindicate the arable in question at their own entire risk and cost, whereas, however, His Most Serene Highness renounces all claims against the purchasers should they in fact win these Skladen of arable, whether wholly or in part, against the burghership of Warta.

4. The delivery of this sold estate to the purchasers shall take place 14 days after Johanni a. c., at which same time and place the first instalment of the 4000 rtll. must be paid, since until this be done the delivery cannot take place.

5. At this delivery there shall be handed over together with it that [uncertain: ground stock] and cattle and implements which are found upon the estate

and is specified in the judicial deed of delivery [Uebergabe-Receß] on the part of the lessee Knoblauch to v. Bloch of Blotniz of the 10th and 11th of July a. p., exclusive of the plus Inventarii in horses and oxen taken away at that time by Knoblauch pursuant to the Receß of the 11th of July, which for that very reason are no longer to be found upon the estate and for that same reason cannot be handed over with it.

6. The Herr Seller promises to procure the consent to the acquisition of this estate for the purchasers, if possible at the latest by Johann a. c.; should the same, however, not be forthcoming, then the purchase in question falls to the ground.

7. Should the Final Resolution concerning the consent in question be delayed longer than 14 days beyond Johann a. c., in such wise that the delivery shall already have taken place and the first instalment of the purchase price shall already have been paid, but the resolution in question should then turn out in the negative

in the negative, then the contracting parties have, for the avoidance of all [uncertain: disputes] concerning the revenues drawn, agreed as follows: that the purchasers shall retain this estate in possession by way of lease for one year, namely until 14 days after St. Johanni 1804, but shall in return pay to the Herr Seller for this year a lease-sum of 800 rtl., say eight hundred Reichsthaler; likewise shall discharge all public dues concerning this estate, by whatever name they may be called, upon the [uncertain: Competenz ex Propriet], without being permitted to bring anything to the Herr Seller's account therefor; and the purchasers renounce, for this last case, each and every remission and other demand whatsoever, by whatever name they may be called, but bind themselves, upon the readiest execution, to vacate the estate of Witow 14 days after Johann 1804 in good husbandly condition, and submit themselves in this

behalf to the executive process with all its legal consequences; it being however understood of itself that in this case, upon the vacating of the estate, the 4000 rtl. paid must be repaid to them by the Herr Seller, after deduction of the [uncertain: stipulated] lease-pension of 800 rt and of those public dues and costs which they could not prove to have been paid at their departure.

8. [uncertain: Furthermore] the estate is handed over to the purchasers with the winter and summer sowing fully put in, and the purchasers hereby declare that they accept the winter sowing as duly sown, and only await the like in respect of the summer sowing.

9. The documents concerning this estate shall, immediately upon the arrival of the consent, be handed out to them for their [uncertain: purpose of acquisition].

10.

10. Finally the contracting parties renounce all objections and evasions running counter to this Punctation of purchase, by whatever name they may be called, in particular the purchasers renounce the plea of injury in and above the half [laesio enormis]; and they set, for the case of non-observance or non-performance of this contract, a vadium or conventional penalty of 1000 rtll., say one thousand Reichsthaler, which the contravening party shall be bound to pay to the other, and nevertheless to perform the contract.

11. The costs of this contract both parties assume by halves; those of the rectification of the Titulus Possessionis in the purchasers' names, the latter alone.

Both parties have, this Punctation of purchase having been read by themselves, which was explained to the co-purchaser v. Kwasiborski by his socius Honricht in the Polish tongue, after previous

previous approval, executed the same with their own hand-written signatures.

Kalisch, the 21st of April 1803.

[uncertain: Upon] the signing both parties remarked to me that, in respect of the buildings standing upon the Schultisey, which the lessees there claim to have built themselves, no Eviction warranty is granted to the purchasers by the Herr Seller; rather, in case the lessees' statement should be correct, the purchasers must come to a separate settlement with them thereupon.

Done as above.

Christian Friedrich Rochlitz
Martin Honrichs

Walęty v Kwasiborski

Carl Anton Grimm

Stanisław Szymanowski

as witness.

The 6000 rl., six thousand Reichsthaler of purchase money payable to me, according to the foregoing Punctation of purchase, at the term of Christmas of this year, and likewise, out of the 6000 rt payable at the term of Johannis 1804, a sum of two thousand Reichsthaler, with priority before the residue, also with all rights

and without novation, and with the pledge-right to be stipulated in the instrument of purchase hereafter to be drawn up and to be intabulated upon the entry of the title of possession, and with interest at 5 per cent from Johannis of this year onward — these I hereby cede to the banker here, Herr Carl Ferdinand Weigel. I acknowledge having received the valuta of this cession from him in cash and in full.

I also promise to procure for Herr Banker Weigel the debtors' consent to this cession as soon as possible. Breslau, the 26th of April 1803. Friedrich Ludwig Fürst zu Hohenlohe. Read and approved by myself.

The foregoing cession, receipt for the valuta and promise to procure the consent of the debitores I accept in the name and as partner of my father Carl Ferdinand Weigel. Breslau, the 26th of April 1803. I have read and approved this. Carl Gottlieb Weigel, in [uncertain: the name] and as partner of [uncertain: my] father Carl Ferdinand Weigel.

That the foregoing cession and receipt for the

valuta, by His Most Serene Highness Herr Friedrich Ludewig reigning Fürst zu Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen, and the acceptation declared by Herr Merchant Carl Gottlieb Weigel in the name and as partner of his father Herr Carl Ferdinand Weigel, were under this day's date executed before the Justice Office of the Ladies' Princely Chapter of St. Vincenz, to which the same are personally well known, after due perusal and declared approval, by their own hand-written signatures and appended seals, as well upon this original Punctation as upon the vidimated copy of the same issued to the Herr Cessionarius — is hereby attested on the ground of the protocol [uncertain: ..ors] taken thereupon. Breslau, the 26th of April 1803. The Justice Office of the Free Princely Chapter of Vincenz.

[L. S.]

Büchler

Finally the contracting parties renounce all objections and evasions running counter to this Punctation of purchase, by whatever name they may be called, in particular the purchasers renounce the plea of injury in and above the half [laesio enormis]; and they set, for the case of non-observance or non-performance of this contract, a vadium or conventional penalty of 1000 rtll., say one thousand Reichsthaler, which the contravening party shall be bound to pay to the other, and nevertheless to perform the contract.

11. The costs of this contract both parties assume by halves; those of the rectification of the Titulus Possessionis in the purchasers' names, the latter alone.

Both parties have, this Punctation of purchase having been read by themselves, which was explained to the co-purchaser v. Kwasiborski by his socius Honricht in the Polish tongue, after previous

previous approval, executed the same with their own hand-written signatures.

Kalisch, the 21st of April 1803.

[uncertain: Upon] the signing both parties remarked to me that, in respect of the buildings standing upon the Schultisey, which the lessees there claim to have built themselves, no Eviction warranty is granted to the purchasers by the Herr Seller; rather, in case the lessees' statement should be correct, the purchasers must come to a separate settlement with them thereupon.

Done as above.

Christian Friedrich Rochlitz
Martin Honrichs

Walęty v Kwasiborski

Carl Anton Grimm

Stanisław Szymanowski

as witness.

The 6000 rl., six thousand Reichsthaler of purchase money payable to me, according to the foregoing Punctation of purchase, at the term of Christmas of this year, and likewise, out of the 6000 rt payable at the term of Johannis 1804, a sum of two thousand Reichsthaler, with priority before the residue, also with all rights

and without novation, and with the pledge-right to be stipulated in the instrument of purchase hereafter to be drawn up and to be intabulated upon the entry of the title of possession, and with interest at 5 per cent from Johannis of this year onward — these I hereby cede to the banker here, Herr Carl Ferdinand Weigel. I acknowledge having received the valuta of this cession from him in cash and in full.

I also promise to procure for Herr Banker Weigel the debtors' consent to this cession as soon as possible. Breslau, the 26th of April 1803. Friedrich Ludwig Fürst zu Hohenlohe. Read and approved by myself.

The foregoing cession, receipt for the valuta and promise to procure the consent of the debitores I accept in the name and as partner of my father Carl Ferdinand Weigel. Breslau, the 26th of April 1803. I have read and approved this. Carl Gottlieb Weigel, in [uncertain: the name] and as partner of [uncertain: my] father Carl Ferdinand Weigel.

That the foregoing cession and receipt for the

valuta, by His Most Serene Highness Herr Friedrich Ludewig reigning Fürst zu Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen, and the acceptation declared by Herr Merchant Carl Gottlieb Weigel in the name and as partner of his father Herr Carl Ferdinand Weigel, were under this day's date executed before the Justice Office of the Ladies' Princely Chapter of St. Vincenz, to which the same are personally well known, after due perusal and declared approval, by their own hand-written signatures and appended seals, as well upon this original Punctation as upon the vidimated copy of the same issued to the Herr Cessionarius — is hereby attested on the ground of the protocol [uncertain: ..ors] taken thereupon. Breslau, the 26th of April 1803. The Justice Office of the Free Princely Chapter of Vincenz.

summary_en: Punctation of purchase in which Forest Inspector Christian Friedrich Rochlitz, acting for Fürst Friedrich Ludwig zu Hohenlohe-Ingelfingen, sells the village and Scholtisey Witow in the Kalisch department, Warta district, to Martin Honrichs and Walęty v. Kwasiborski for 16,000 Reichsthaler in instalments, with no Eviction warranty for 1016 Skladen claimed by the burghership of Warta, a fallback one-year lease at 800 rtl., and a 1000 rtl. penalty; appended is the Fürst's cession of 8000 rtl. of the purchase money to banker Carl Ferdinand Weigel, attested at Breslau by the Justice Office of the Chapter of St. Vincenz.
summary_de: Punctation über den Verkauf des adeligen Gutes Witow (Dorf und Scholtisey, Departement Kalisch, Kreis Warta) durch Forstinspektor Christian Friedrich Rochlitz als Bevollmächtigten des Fürsten an Martin Honrichs und Walęty v. Kwasiborski für 16000 Rthl in Raten (4000 zu Johannis, 6000 Weihnachten, 6000 Johanni 1804, 5 Prozent Zinsen), ohne Eviktionsleistung für 1016 Skladen streitiger Äcker der Bürgerschaft Warta; Vadium 1000 Rthl, Verzicht auf laesio enormis, Übergabe mit Winter- und Sommersaat, ersatzweise Pacht zu 800 Rthl. Angefügt Cession von 8000 Rthl an Bankier Carl Ferdinand Weigel, beglaubigt vom Justizamt des Stifts St. Vincenz.
